aiOverview.content: The U.S. Space Force (USSF) is the newest branch of the U.S. Armed Forces, established on December 20, 2019, to secure, protect, and defend national interests in, from, and to space. Headquartered at the Pentagon, it trains and equips "Guardians" to manage GPS satellites, track space debris, and provide global satellite communication capabilities. This video provides an overview of the U.S. Space Force's mission and its role in protecting national security:55sUnited States Space ForceYouTube• May 1, 2025 55s Key Aspects of the U.S. Space Force: Mission: Organize, train, and equip forces to ensure freedom of action in space, enhance joint combat capabilities, and defend against space-based threats. Location: While headquartered at the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., the Space Force operates from multiple bases and installations worldwide, including Peterson Space Force Base in Colorado. Guardians & Culture: Members are called Guardians, a name rooted in historical space command, aimed at creating a dedicated, forward-thinking, and agile force. Operations & Scope: The force focuses on orbital warfare, electromagnetic warfare, and space situational awareness to protect American assets and, in some cases, support civilian efforts like the Artemis II mission. Joining & Benefits: Eligible individuals (ages 18–41, or 17 with consent) can join as Enlisted Guardians or officers, with training held at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas. Benefits include competitive salaries, comprehensive insurance, and education assistance. For more information, you can visit the official U.S. Space Force website. U.S. Space Force website
